title: Superman Aesthetics Bodybuilding Program (Henry Cavill Physique Workout)
summary: A three-day upper/lower/full-body intermediate program plus an optional Sunday accessory day, built to recreate Henry Cavill's Superman physique naturally. It prioritizes chest, shoulders, traps, biceps and abs, gives medium focus to lats, upper back, neck, forearms and quads, and expects a lean bulk at around 15% body fat.
claims: Henry Cavill's physique is achievable naturally with proper training; he may be gifted in frame and possibly enhanced, but his dedication suggests it could be natural
Plan your training around your dream body: Cavill's look is a massive shoulder girdle where delts, chest and traps connect, so those are the main focus
Superman needs big biceps; triceps matter less because the look is defined from the front

Priorities: high focus chest, shoulders, traps, biceps, abs; medium focus lats, upper back, neck (at least connecting to the jawline), forearms, quads; low focus triceps, glutes, hamstrings, calves, rear delts
Cavill looks massive because he is bear mode at relatively high body fat, not shredded; he himself is 15%+ body fat with abs and veins thanks to muscle mass
To be that big you must slow bulk and accept slightly higher body fat; it is more sustainable and lets you put energy into the gym
The program is for intermediates; novices who run it will crash and burn
Within each day respect the pyramid of intensity and priority: first sets most important, so if you must skip something skip the last
In giant sets order the movements from most to least intense (e.g. overhead press, then curl, then decline sit-up), then rest 3-4 minutes

Monday upper: bench/dips/weighted push-ups 4x4-10 + DB or machine rows 4x6-12; OHP 3-4x6-10 + DB/EZ curls 3-4x8-12 + decline sit-ups 3-4x10-15; cable flies or bent-arm pec deck 4x12-15 + upright rows or lateral raises 4x10-15 + reverse or hammer curls 4x8-12
After a compound press plus a shoulder isolation, more shoulder work that day is junk volume

Wednesday lower: BB or Zercher squat 3x6-8 or belt/hack squat or leg press 4x6-12 + neck extensions 4x10-15; RDL or block pulls 3-4x8-12 + behind-the-back cable curls 3-4x10-12 + seated calf raises 3-4x15-20; lat pulldowns 4x8-12 or weighted pull-ups 4x6-8 + DB or upper-chest shrugs 4x12-15 + French press or behind-the-head cable extension 4x10-12
Machine squats (belt, hack, leg press) allow more sets than barbell squats because of less systemic and spinal fatigue
Exercise choices can be rotated week A/week B (e.g. RDLs one week, block pulls the next)
Prioritize weighted pull-ups over the RDL line; if you skip something skip the second line
Growing the triceps long head pushes the biceps upward and makes the biceps look bigger

Friday full body: incline or Viking press 3-4x6-12 + Kroc rows or DB pullovers 3-4x8-12; farmer's carry 3x30 m or trap bar deadlift 3x6-10 + cable lateral raises or incline cable flies 3x12-15 + Russian twists or leg raises 3x15-20; then lower twist (leg extensions or split squats 4x15-20) or upper twist (machine/DB chest press 4x8-12), plus pinwheel or hammer curls 4x10-12 and neck flexions 4x10-15
At intermediate level progression needs wide rep ranges so you can accumulate reps at the same weight, not only add load
Bodybuilding programs avoid 2-3 rep maxes; they have a place but not here
Ab isolation is non-negotiable if you want a six-pack while staying at higher body fat; it is what makes bear mode look good

Optional Sunday: standing or seated calf raises 6-10x10-20 + neck flexions and extensions 6-10x10-25; shrugs 3-4x15-20 + band triceps extensions 3-4 sets of 30-50 not to failure for elbow health; planks 3x1 min; plus low-impact activity like hiking, swimming or biking
Light band triceps extensions pump blood and synovial fluid into the elbow to prevent tendinitis from heavy pressing
exercises: posterior chain with little lower back stress
